title: Study Skills and Exam Preparation for Matric
summary: Planning a matric study timetable, evidence-based study strategies, understanding question verbs and cognitive levels, exam-writing techniques, and managing exam stress.

items: List all assessment dates: tests, assignments, prelims and final exams.
Draw up a **term plan** and a **weekly timetable** with fixed study time for each subject.
Plan revision in cycles: learn, review after a day, a week and a month (**spaced practice**).
Build in rest, exercise and sleep.

rows: Test yourself without notes; use past papers and flash cards
Revisit topics several times over weeks
Mix question types in one session
Explain why and how; connect ideas
Combine words with diagrams, timelines and mind maps
Show understanding in your own words
Use knowledge in a new situation
Analyse, compare, critically discuss, evaluate, justify
Break down information, weigh evidence and give a reasoned judgement

items: Use reading time to plan: note marks and choose questions where there is a choice.
Budget time by marks: in a 3-hour paper worth 150 marks, allow about 1,2 minutes per mark.
Answer what is asked; underline key words.
Show working and structure long answers with an introduction, body and conclusion.

notes.label: Exam stress
notes.text: Prepare early, sleep well before exams, eat breakfast, arrive early, and use slow breathing if you panic. If a question seems impossible, move on and return to it later.

questions.prompt: Testing yourself without looking at notes is called…
Match each verb to its cognitive level.
Spaced practice means revising a topic several times over a period of weeks.
What is the strategy of combining words with diagrams and visuals called? (two words)
Give THREE features of a good matric study timetable.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): includes all subjects; based on assessment dates; spaced revision; realistic; includes breaks, sleep and exercise; reviewed regularly

questions.prompt: What is expected in an answer to an 'evaluate' question?
questions.memo:
✓ Weigh up evidence or arguments (1)
✓ and give a reasoned judgement or conclusion (1)
Any three (1 each): plan during reading time; budget time by marks; underline key words; answer what is asked; structure long answers; check work

questions.prompt: What should you do if you cannot answer a question in an exam?
questions.memo:
✓ Move on to other questions so you do not lose time (1)
✓ Return to it later; write what you know for partial marks (1)

questions.prompt: Explain interleaving and why it helps in Mathematics.
questions.memo:
✓ Mixing different types of problems in one session (1)
✓ It trains you to choose the right method, as in an exam (1)

questions.prompt: Why are preliminary examinations important for Grade 12 learners?
questions.memo:
✓ They give practice under exam conditions (1)
✓ and show weak areas to focus on before the final exams (1)
